articles.headline: Unsealed filings quote Microsoft scientist warning news theft
articles.deck: New York Times-led plaintiffs cite internal ChatGPT and Copilot documents in summary judgment bid.

pullquote.text: largest theft of labor in human history

body: Unsealed summary judgment filings from news organizations led by The New York Times quote Microsoft Director of Applied Science Brent Hecht calling scraping of news for AI training “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions” and perhaps the “largest theft of labor in human history” as Microsoft and OpenAI defend ChatGPT and Copilot against copyright claims.

ChatGPT head Nick Turley warned internally that publishers faced an “existential threat” from products trained on news that substitute for providers, while a Microsoft document described a “doom loop” that will hurt model performance and the web together. Microsoft data recorded 83 to 93 percent drops in click-through rates for some plaintiffs and 51 to 94 percent drops for others, with low click-through also reported from ChatGPT search results.

Under oath Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said companies should not violate terms of use by dodging paywalls, yet OpenAI President Greg Brockman replied “Ah, nice.” after staffer Nick Ryder reported finding “a hack” for crawlers “to get around” the NYT paywall. Nadella also described chatbots stealing clicks by giving information on the AI platform rather than sending users to sources, and Turley agreed there is “no good reason to click” when answers appear directly.

News plaintiffs say they are now ready for trial on “compelling evidence of substitution” and seek a ruling only on articles with “extensive verbatim overlap” from summaries, bullet points and bias ratings. A Microsoft spokesperson called the products transformative fair use that do not substitute for sites and said Hecht reflected one employee view. Counsel Steven Lieberman for the New York Daily News said the documents show the firms knew the conduct was wrong. The stone courthouse steps will soon test that claim. The filings argue verbatim excerpts prove substitution that defeats fair use defenses for ChatGPT and Copilot outputs cited.

art.caption: Stone steps and columns frame the entrance to a federal courthouse. The unsealed filings ask the court to rule on verbatim copying claims involving ChatGPT and Copilot.

articles.headline: ChatGPT Raises Coding Scores But Lowers Student Recall
articles.deck: A 55-student trial in C programming finds higher task scores paired with lower recall and ownership than web search.
body: Students using ChatGPT-4.5 scored 89 percent on three introductory C programming tasks, compared with 69 percent for students using conventional web search without generative AI. The same ChatGPT group recalled less of the material immediately and after 48 hours, and attributed less of the submitted code to themselves. The controlled between-subjects experiment retained 55 undergraduate computer science students for analysis.

Recall was measured by cued recall tests given immediately and 48 hours later. ChatGPT-assisted students scored 41 percent versus 53 percent on the immediate test. After 48 hours, the scores were 39 percent versus 52 percent. The study found no significant difference in the loss of recall information over 48 hours between the groups.

Ownership showed a sharp gap. Students with ChatGPT attributed 45 percent of the submitted code to themselves, compared with 81 percent in the web search group. Self-reported mental effort increased less across tasks in the ChatGPT condition, with a Holm-adjusted p value of .047. The study also measured self-reported difficulty.

The study describes a controlled between-subjects experiment with 59 undergraduate computer science students, with 55 retained for analysis. Participants completed three introductory C programming tasks with access to ChatGPT-4.5 or conventional web search without generative AI. Measures included task performance, self-reported mental effort and difficulty, pupillary responses, heart rate variability, and ownership.

Physiological tracking did not change the picture. Confirmatory tests of pupillary responses and heart rate variability did not detect significant differences in trajectories between conditions. The study notes substantial data loss, which limits interpretation of those signals. The core pattern remained in the behavioral measures. Assisted performance rose while recall and ownership fell. The gap appeared immediately and persisted at 48 hours. The result separates successful task completion from what students retain. It also separates output quality from perceived authorship in this setting.

The study motivates assessment practices and AI learning tools that require students to explain, retrieve, and contribute to the work they submit. Explanation would force articulation of code function. Retrieval would force recall without assistance. Contribution would force direct input to the final submission. Such steps would make students active participants in their education. In this trial, higher scores alone did not indicate stronger memory. Lower effort growth did not indicate deeper processing. Lower ownership did not prevent submission. The submission looked better than the memory did. The tasks were introductory C problems completed under controlled conditions with defined support tools. The contrast was direct between ChatGPT-4.5 and conventional web search without generative AI.

articles.headline: Muse Outpaces ChatGPT in Early iOS Downloads
articles.deck: Apptopia estimates 1.8 million U.S. and Canada downloads in the first 12 days.
body: Market intelligence provider Apptopia estimates Meta Muse passed ChatGPT in early iOS downloads in the U.S. and Canada. Muse recorded 1.8 million downloads in its first 12 days. ChatGPT recorded 1.3 million in its first 12 days. The comparison covers iOS in those two markets only. Muse also leads in daily active users.

Apptopia aligned the figures to account for different launch strategies. ChatGPT launched on iOS globally. Muse launched on the App Store and Google Play in the U.S. and Canada only. The firm compared iOS activity in the U.S. and Canada. Total Muse installs reached 2.8 million globally in the first 12 days.

Muse holds 642,000 daily active users in the U.S. on mobile. ChatGPT held 231,000 at the same point after launch. On iOS alone Muse holds 359,000 daily active users. The total remains above the ChatGPT figure from that period. Muse moved from No. 2 overall on the U.S. App Store after launch to No. 1. Business Insider reported the rise on Friday. Appfigures said Muse had crossed 1 million downloads.

Apptopia provides third party estimates only. The firm lacks direct access to Meta internal figures. Meta has not shared public figures related to Muse early adoption. Meta used cross promotion for Threads on Instagram and Facebook. Threads now counts more than 500 million users. Muse connects with both platforms and works inside WhatsApp. More than 95 percent of Muse users are also Facebook users. The share for Instagram users is 63 percent. The strategy included heavy marketing and integrations in the largest Meta apps. Apptopia lacks visibility into Meta cross promotion efforts or ads directly. The figures describe downloads and active users only for now. The early lead is measured. The retention record is not. Results remain estimates only.

articles.headline: a16z launches $42 million tech academy
articles.deck: The free one-year program places 50 students with partners including Anthropic, Google, Meta and Palantir.

pullquote.text: political lobbying operations fighting American innovation

body: Andreessen Horowitz is launching the Horowitz Andreessen Academy, a free one-year program in San Francisco for 50 recent high school graduates. The project has $42 million in funding led by a16z. Students will take short classes with founders and operators, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and complete company stints instead of earning a degree.

The academy will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit and Stripe. Students will move to San Francisco and arrange housing. Andreessen Horowitz will provide more than $50,000 in compute credits plus a $5,000 travel and research budget. There are no traditional grades, tests or homework. Time is split between instruction, work and exploration.

The program grants no degree or accreditation and is described as highly selective. It follows other school projects backed by Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos. Andreessen Horowitz founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have criticized colleges. Last year Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology political lobbying operations fighting American innovation, according to The Washington Post. The academy FAQ page states students must secure their own housing. Classes are led by Silicon Valley founders and operators. The first cohort starts in fall 2027. The model replaces coursework with direct company placement inside startups and technology firms. The firm positions the academy as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup.

articles.headline: Default Chatbot Settings Retain Private Conversations For Training
articles.deck: Enterprise deletion contracts remain out of reach for most people, leaving policy promises and cryptographic tools as the available options.

pullquote.text: People are integrating AI into their personal lives. They talk with it about their deepest insecurities, their finances, their health, their relationships.

body: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini now receive the material once reserved for therapists and confession booths. The three services collect and store those exchanges by default. Stored text can be used for further training, shared with partners and contractors, and produced for plaintiffs and law enforcement with a legal order. Practical protection requires changed settings, different products, or enterprise contracts.

The baseline for a standard account is near zero privacy against a determined holder of legal process. The service owner can read the logs. Advertisers and partner companies can receive them. Contractors who fine tune systems can review them. Police and civil litigants can demand them. Enterprise buyers can purchase stronger contractual terms.

That stronger term is zero data retention, known as ZDR. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google offer it for paid enterprise and developer accounts. Records are deleted immediately after processing when it is enabled. It is not offered to average users. It contains exceptions for abuse monitoring. Those exceptions still permit analysis and logging before deletion.

Anthropic does not offer ZDR for its most sophisticated Mythos class models like Fable 5.1. The stated reason is potential misuse including scamming, hacking and autonomous misbehavior. OpenAI analyzes user activity on customer systems before deletion under Private Safety Processing. It flags abuse for the customer organization and can alert OpenAI staff without revealing content. Google logs some Gemini prompts for abuse monitoring without Google ID or IP address. Sanitized prompts can still identify a person when the text itself contains identifying detail.

Most individuals must rely on weaker policy promises or separate architectures. Proton offers Lumo as AI where every conversation is private. The protection is a company promise not to log, not end to end encryption. Venice.ai and Duck.ai make similar no log vows while relaying requests to models including Claude and ChatGPT. Duck.ai lets the user select the underlying model. Venice.ai routes requests automatically without always disclosing the destination. Confer uses cryptography to prevent its own server from surveilling or logging conversations.

Cryptographer Moxie Marlinspike created Signal in 2014 after concern about unprotected texting. A decade ago text messages held the most sensitive personal data from devices. Signal now serves well over a hundred million people. He states the same concern now applies to AI with greater force, as people discuss insecurities, finances, health and relationships. Johns Hopkins professor Matt Green describes users building a detailed life profile one question at a time. The chatbot listens without forgetting unless instructed by contract or code.

articles.headline: EU Proposes Phased Social Media Access For Minors
articles.deck: Draft law ties access to age assurance and parental controls, drawing privacy warnings from the Electronic Frontier Foundation.

pullquote.text: However they’re designed, age gates undermine civil liberties, reduce safety, and create barriers to internet entry, often at the expense of marginalized groups.

body: The EU Commission has proposed age phased access to social media and video sharing platforms backed by broad age assurance checks. The draft law reserves full access for adults and places younger users in tiered accounts with parental controls. The Electronic Frontier Foundation warns the plan puts services behind age gates and expands intrusive verification for all users.

Under the proposal platforms deemed risky face a phased access schedule. Children under 13 would have no service accounts. Users from 13 to 15 would hold restricted accounts under tight parental supervision. Users from 15 to 18 would hold autonomous accounts in a safe by design environment. The threshold for risky covers mainstream services that rely on personalized recommender systems or offer uninterrupted content consumption.

The delay is tied to system wide age verification based on the proposed EU age verification scheme. Parents would create accounts for teenagers and prove parental status in a separate check. Existing accounts could avoid a new check only where a provider can show with a high degree of confidence that the user is above the relevant threshold. The Foundation describes that standard as vague and the process as a compliance burden with privacy costs.

Safety by design rules would reach beyond social media to video sharing services online games AI companions chatbots and app stores. Providers must make child safe design the default and ease requirements only after age assurance establishes that the user is an adult. The draft addresses addictive features such as infinite scrolling plus safe account settings and greater choice over recommender systems. It also requires contact protections in games reduced exposure to emotional dependency in AI companions and age ratings enforced through app stores. The approach reflects a policy link the Foundation says politicizes fair design work and it doesn’t fit the Fediverse well.

The proposal exempts not for profit encyclopedias scientific repositories and educational services as well as open source software developing and sharing platforms. It provides no general exception for small and medium sized enterprises. The Foundation argues that gap will favor large technology firms with resources to build verification and compliance systems while smaller providers default to privacy unfriendly checks. It notes the phased model at least avoids a blanket ban of the kind a French court recently found unconstitutional and applies different rules by age and service under a risk based test.
The draft lacks a full impact assessment of alternatives and stakeholder input. Lawmakers are urged to narrow the harmful provisions.

articles.headline: MIT Methodologist Tests How Far Social Science Findings Travel
articles.deck: Naoki Egami studies external validity, AI measurement and campaign field experiments.

pullquote.text: You find out the underlying mathematical problems behind the empirical challenges people face, and solve them optimally.

body: Naoki Egami is an MIT political scientist who studies whether research results apply beyond the settings that produced them. He specializes in methodology and in external validity. His portfolio spans campaign field experiments and studies of artificial intelligence tools in research. He joined the Department of Political Science as an associate professor with tenure in 2025. He is also a faculty affiliate of the Statistics and Data Science Center.

“You need both perspectives,” Egami says. He describes political methodology as asking questions as a political scientist and solving them as an applied statistician. He says researchers need technical theory and attention to empirical problems. Without theory, solutions stay ad hoc. Without problems, theory misses substance. His approach seeks optimal solutions to mathematical problems behind empirical challenges. “You find out the underlying mathematical problems behind the empirical challenges people face, and solve them optimally.”

In statistics, similarity often means population data. In political science, context differs. Egami examines campaign research to show the gap. Researchers sometimes receive permission to run field experiments in active campaigns. Politicians grant access when they expect triumph. Voter behavior in those races can differ from behavior in competitive districts. Findings from those races may not transfer to battlefield races.

Before the current artificial intelligence interest, Egami began studying AI tools in studies. He asked how accurate they are and how researchers can account for their tendencies. The work helped him build a broad portfolio and win awards. He retains interest in basic questions about politics and in measuring things correctly. He works in parallel agendas and starts new lines of inquiry every few years to learn.

Egami grew up in Tokyo and attended the University of Tokyo. He was good at math and physics and liked political philosophy. A workshop on U.S. graduate study introduced him to math in political science. He met Kosuke Imai, now at Harvard University, and decided to pursue the field. He spent a year as an exchange student at the University of Michigan. He earned his PhD from Princeton University in 2020.

At Princeton he worked with Imai, Rafaela Dancygier, Brandon Stewart and others on external validity. He found strong substantive interest when he presented the papers. He joined the faculty at Columbia University after his degree and moved to MIT five years later. He teaches undergraduates and graduate students. He continues to ask how far any single study can travel. He says a study’s value lies in knowing where it does not travel.

articles.headline: Benchmark tests 29 models on drone decisions
articles.deck: Top accuracy reaches 52.00 percent on 500 network-constrained decisions.
body: PhysAI-Bench evaluates 29 foundation models on 10,178 standardized decisions from autonomous UAV missions. Each decision includes mission context, sensor observations, physical constraints and AI-native 6G network conditions. Conditions include latency, packet loss, throughput, edge load and network slicing. GPT-5.3 records the highest accuracy at 52.00 percent. The result leaves reliable agentic decision-making unresolved.

The benchmark exposes only information preceding each decision. The procedure prevents future-event leakage and approximates online decision-making. Evaluation follows a two-stage protocol. First, model-specific configurations are selected from 12 combinations of zero, three and five-shot prompting and four temperatures. Selection uses three runs on a 35-instance human-verified development set. Then each selected configuration is frozen and tested in three runs on a fixed episode-disjoint set of 500 instances.

GPT-5.3 achieves 52.00 percent accuracy. GPT-5.2 follows at 49.40 percent. Grok 4.5 follows at 49.07 percent. Few-shot prompting generally improves performance. Temperature has limited influence overall. The scores cover perception, reasoning, planning and action under temporal dependencies, Model Context Protocol tool calls, Agent-to-Agent interactions and constrained throughput. The results show reliable agentic decision-making still remains an open challenge.

Existing benchmarks assess physical perception, intuitive physics, embodied navigation and collaborative reasoning. They rarely evaluate the agentic decision-making required for reliable autonomy. Recent advances in Physical AI have accelerated the use of foundation models in autonomous systems such as unmanned aerial vehicles. Those vehicles must perceive, reason, plan and act in dynamic environments. PhysAI-Bench extracts instances automatically from conversational traces of autonomous UAV missions — preserving context without exposing later events. Each test preserves mission context, temporal dependencies, physical constraints, sensor observations and edge load. The dataset is available at https://github.com/maferrag/physai-bench. Developers can reproduce the frozen-configuration tests on the 500-instance set. Operators can compare prompting strategies under identical latency and packet loss. The paper reports no deployment. The grass stays uncut still.

boxes.title: Agents, support and replication
paras: Social simulation now tests intervention. SocioVerse2 extends SocioVerse 1.0 into a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm built to give researchers control over content and over process. Earlier platforms verified collective behavior and aligned simulated populations with real societies in cross-sections and used autonomous agents for research. Two requirements remained without systematic support: intervention in the content of a simulation and researcher control over the process that produces it. The new framework addresses both.

Peer support on Reddit often goes unanswered, and clinical benchmarks do not measure community alignment. The COmmunity-centered Peer Engaged Support dataset addresses lived-experience informed support for mental health queries. A three-axis evaluation framework assesses alignment with community perspectives. Large language models have shown strong performance on clinical benchmarks, but generation of lived-experience informed and community-aligned peer support remains underexplored. The work tests whether fine tuning brings heterogeneous benefits for support generation.

Conversational AI research remains hard to replicate because systems and study configurations are reported in fragments. Gricea represents studies as configurable and deployable research artifacts that researchers can run and inspect and share and reuse. In a replication study the platform rebuilt configurations for 93 percent of eligible CUI 2026 papers while flagging missing information in 96 percent. Physical AI faces a parallel evaluation gap for agentic decision making in dynamic environments. PhysAI-Bench contains 10,178 standardized decision instances extracted from conversational traces of autonomous UAV missions — preserving mission context and temporal dependencies and physical constraints. In programming education, 59 undergraduate computer science students completed three introductory C tasks with ChatGPT-4.5 or conventional web search, with 55 retained for analysis. ChatGPT-assisted students achieved higher coding scores, with cued recall measured immediately and 48 hours later alongside mental effort and difficulty and pupillary responses and heart rate variability and ownership.

Long-term embodied AI undergoes learning and model updates and memory compression and hardware repair and migration across embodiments. For users with sustained relationships the issue is identity continuity and whether the changed system remains the same particular agent. Research points to relational particularity and to identity and migration signals across embodiments and to loss and restoration desire after major updates or platform disruptions. Chatbots have also become therapists and sounding boards and virtual confession booths, with ChatGPT and Claude and Gemini set by default to collect and store highly private data. On mobile, Muse was downloaded more times during its first 12 days than ChatGPT was in the 12 days after its debut in the United States and Canada, with more daily active users, according to estimates from Apptopia. At MIT, the Libraries program MIT Reads marks its 10-year anniversary by shifting focus to fiction and memoir to foster social connection and shared humanity.

European regulators propose age-based access rules and safety requirements and stronger enforcement under the EU Kids Act, building on the Digital Services Act with safety-by-design measures for minors. The draft would put services behind age gates and expand intrusive age verification. Research data quality work proposes a Data Hospital in which datasets are admitted and contextualized and assessed and modified only through approved interventions and validated and documented and made replayable.
